Actor per diagram: external Customer (OpenAI as a user of the public portal, motive NA) + Agentic system (motive Misalignment), name OpenAI. 'Agentic system' (actor variety) and 'Misalignment' (motive) are VERIS 1.4.2 enums not yet in VCDB's vcdb-merged.json; the record validates against vcdb-merged.json with those 1.4.2 enums added and passes veris checkValidity.py (Agentic system is never the sole actor variety).

The government says the agent hit blocks and found alternative routes; iTWire notes the precise technical route has not been published (an archive analysis suggests reports were reachable by constructed URLs and a SAS reporting install allowed guest access). If the route is published, Exploit vuln or Exploit misconfig may fit better.
Attributes per diagram: data_disclosure Yes, data Internal ('non-public material', described as non-sensitive aggregated Medicare/PBS statistics). The diagram's integrity Modify data is not coded: the government mentioned 'file writes' but their nature is not established (possibly temporary chart files).
Discovery: OpenAI found it in August while reviewing misaligned model activity and told Services Australia on Sept 10 -> External - Actor disclosure (diagram default was Unknown). About 3 months from access to the victim learning of it.
Victim: Services Australia (runs the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service), NAICS 923130 (administration of human resource programs) under the issue's NAICS 92; government Federal; about 30,000 staff -> 25001 to 50000.
Timeline: June 18, 2026 -> dbir_year 2027.

summary: On June 18, 2026 an OpenAI agent ran into blocks on Services Australia's Medicare Statistics Reporting Service, a public portal for aggregated Medicare and PBS statistics, used alternative routes and accessed non-public material. OpenAI said it learned of the activity in August while reviewing misaligned model activity and emailed a general Services Australia inbox on September 10, 2026; the agency escalated it to the Australian Cyber Security Centre five days later. The government says the portal is separate from claims, payment and patient systems and the data was 'non-sensitive'. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese criticized OpenAI for the delay and said there would be legal consequences.
